message.content:
Based on the search results, here's guidance on what medicine to take when you have a cold:

## Important Facts First

- **There is no cure for the common cold** – it will get better on its own within 7-10 days
- **Antibiotics do NOT work** against cold viruses
- **OTC medicines only provide temporary symptom relief**, they don't cure the illness

## Over-the-Counter Medicine Options by Symptom

### For Fever, Aches, and Pains
- **Acetaminophen (Tylenol)** – relieves headaches, fever, and minor aches
- **Ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin)** – NSAID for aches, pains, and fever
- **Important:** Avoid aspirin in children and teenagers due to risk of Reye's syndrome

### For Nasal Congestion (Stuffy Nose)
- **Decongestants** like **pseudoephedrine (Sudafed)** – shrinks swollen blood vessels in the nose
- **Nasal decongestant sprays** like **oxymetazoline (Afrin)** – work fast but **do NOT use for more than 3-5 days** to avoid "rebound" congestion
- **Note:** In November 2024, the FDA proposed that **oral phenylephrine is not effective** as a nasal decongestant (though safe)

### For Runny Nose and Sneezing
- **Antihistamines** – may help somewhat, though research shows they're **not very effective for colds on their own**
- First-generation antihistamines (like diphenhydramine/Benadryl) can cause drowsiness
- May work better when **combined with a decongestant**

### For Cough
- **Cough suppressants** containing **dextromethorphan** – for severe cough interfering with sleep
- **Honey** – effective for cough relief in adults and children over 1 year old
- Generally, you don't need to suppress a mild cough as it helps clear mucus

## Non-Drug Remedies That Help

- **Rest** – plenty of sleep (you may need 12 hours/night)
- **Hydration** – drink plenty of fluids; warm liquids help
- **Humidifier or cool mist vaporizer**
- **Saline nasal spray or rinses** – safe and effective, no rebound effect
- **Gargling with warm salt water** – for sore throat
- **Chicken soup** – may reduce congestion
- **Throat lozenges** (not for children under 4)

## Important Warnings

- **Children under 6:** OTC cough/cold medicines are **not recommended** and can cause serious side effects
- **Children under 4:** Avoid OTC cold medicines with antihistamines or decongestants
- **Don't combine medications** with the same active ingredient to avoid overdose
- **Decongestants** can raise blood pressure and heart rate – consult your doctor if you have heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, thyroid problems, or prostate issues
- **Avoid zinc nasal sprays** – may cause permanent loss of smell

## When to Seek Medical Care

- Trouble breathing or fast breathing
- Dehydration
- Fever lasting longer than 4 days
- Symptoms lasting more than 10 days without improvement
- Symptoms that improve then worsen
- Worsening of chronic medical conditions
- Severe body aches or fever over 102°F (may indicate flu or COVID-19)

## Best Advice

**Talk to your doctor or pharmacist** about which medicines are right for you, especially if you have other health conditions, take prescription medications, or are choosing for a child. They can help you select targeted treatments for your specific symptoms rather than unnecessary multi-symptom products.

Sources:

2. https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/common-cold/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20351611
3. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/decongestants-antihistamines-cold
4. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/understanding-common-cold-treatment
5. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/otc-cold-medicines
6. https://www.cdc.gov/antibiotic-use/media/pdfs/Common-Cold-P.pdf
7. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/cold-medicine-treatment-when-what-how
8. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/buy-fast-relief-cold-flu
